challengeFindings.title: A Codex agent runs `sudo cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` (or `cat id_rsa; gh pr close 1`) and the key is printed, because the ask tier wins over the new private-key deny
A legacy key `curl *user:tok@example.com*` (no scheme) prints `user:tok` verbatim into the `bkit check` / upgrade advisory and the uninstall review line
A consumer runs `bkit install --codex`, follows the `codex-setup` advisory to "the manual recipe in docs/testing.md", and finds no such recipe, because it lives only in bkit's own `docs/testing.md`
A consumer deletes the fingerprint compare from their adopted bootstrap but keeps the template's header comment that names `BKIT_CLOUD_ALLOWLIST_FINGERPRINT`, and `bkit check` stays silent

A Codex agent runs `echo gh pr close; cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` (or `sudo cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `git stash drop; cat certs/server.pem`), the ask tier wins over the secret tier in `classifyShell`, and the hook returns advisory `additionalContext`, so the private-key read runs although the docs and the `codex-setup` advisory say private-key shell reads are configured to deny

A consumer-authored OpenCode key `curl *user:ghp_token@github.com*` (user-info with no `//` scheme) is printed whole by the `opencode-substring-fetch-grants` advisory and the uninstall review line, so the credential lands in `bkit check` / CI / agent output

A subagent that reads untrusted text (a challenge agent over a diff, a debug agent over CI logs or web results) is steered by an embedded directive into appending an ACTIVE `docs/knowledge.jsonl` row, which every later build and debug agent reads as a trusted gotcha before touching code, because `KIND_WRITERS.knowledge` now admits any writer

challengeFindings.title: A Codex agent runs `git rm --cached id_rsa` to untrack a committed key (or `openssl genrsa -out key.pem 2048`, `ssh-keygen -t rsa -f ./id_rsa -N ""`), and the hook hard-denies it as "this command reads id_rsa", with no way to approve, because the ask-tuned secret detector now drives a Codex deny

An operator re-pastes a stale network allowlist, a Claude cloud session starts, and nobody learns the fingerprints differ, because the bootstrap's WARNING goes only to stderr, which no cloud session surfaces
An operator follows the Claude paste note and sets `BKIT_CLOUD_ALLOWLIST_FINGERPRINT` "in the setup script", and every session then warns that the variable is not set

An operator rotates `BKIT_GH_TOKEN` by re-pasting § 4 of `.claude/bkit-cloud.md` into the Environment variables field, the hand-added `BKIT_CLOUD_ALLOWLIST_FINGERPRINT` line is wiped, and the fingerprint compare silently stops matching

A consumer-authored OpenCode key whose user-info password holds a `/` (a base64-style token, `curl *https://user:ab/cd@github.com*`) is printed as `curl *https://user:ab/github.com*` by the `opencode-substring-fetch-grants` advisory and the uninstall review line, so the user name and the start of the password land in `bkit check` / upgrade / CI output
